### 📦 Release: v2.0.1 — MH201/MH202 Cover Reversal Fix, SSDP Reload Loop Fix, Climate Startup/Standalone Fixes & 0–10 V Actuator Output Sensor

Patch release **`v2.0.1`** of **MyHOME for Home Assistant** on **[`OWNd 2.0.2`](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/OWNd/releases/tag/v2.0.2)** (**Home Assistant 2026.8+** / Python 3.14).

#### ✨ Features

- **Dark-Mode Brand Assets (`custom_components/myhome/brand/`)**: Bundled `dark_icon.png` (`256×256`), `dark_icon@2x.png` (`512×512`), `dark_logo.png` (`453×128`), and `dark_logo@2x.png` (`907×256`) alongside the light-theme brand PNGs (lossless, sRGB, Adam7-interlaced, transparent-background PNGs with `#F2F2F2` typography and intact Legrand/BTicino accent colors) so Home Assistant's local Brands Proxy API and the 2026.11+ Marketplace render high-contrast artwork in dark mode.
- **Thermoregulation (`WHO = 4`) — Expose `0–10 V` Proportional Actuator Output Level (`Dimension 20` `100..200` → `0..100 %`) ([#949](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/949), [#952](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/952))**: Auto-discovers a per-actuator `%` `SensorEntity` (`MyHOMEActuatorOutputSensor`, `SensorStateClass.MEASUREMENT`) on the zone's Home Assistant device strictly for explicit `Z#N` (`1 <= Z <= 99`, `1 <= N <= 9`) `Dimension 20` proportional codes `100..200` (without requiring bus-wide `generate_events`; no `Z#0` or bare-`Z` level spreading, starts `unknown` after restart until the first bus report rather than restoring stale values, and registers `watch_zone_actuators` when not interface-refused), and exposes `actuator_levels` (`0..100`) on `MyHOMEClimate` (while keeping `actuators` strictly `"on"` / `"off"`) and `output_level` / `actuator_levels` on `MyHOMEThermoSwitch` (all excluded from Home Assistant recorder history via `_unrecorded_attributes` so ramp steps record only on the `sensor`). Thanks to **[@xmavgithub](https://github.com/xmavgithub)** for the live `MyHomeServer1` (`2.87.13`) + `F459` (*HVAC 0-10V FanControl*) + `F430V10` (`0–10 V`) ramp captures!

#### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Protocol Engine Upgrade (`OWNd 2.0.2`) — `MH200N` Energy Discovery (`WHO = 18`) & Command-Session Hardening ([#998](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/998), [`OWNd#184`](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/OWNd/pull/184), [`OWNd#185`](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/OWNd/pull/185), [`OWNd#186`](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/OWNd/pull/186))**: Upgraded `manifest.json` and `pyproject.toml` to `OWNd==2.0.2`: enables `WHO = 18` (`WHO_ENERGY`) and `supports_energy_instant_power = True` on `MH200N` (`003565` / `03565`, backed by live `MH200N` `1.1.8` captures answering `*#18*51*51##` and `010108` `bt_supervisione` firmware oracle verdicts while keeping legacy `MH200` `020102` unchanged), holds `SEND_AUTH_COOLDOWN` (`60 s`) on `OWNCommandSession` after fatal authentication/negotiation refusals (`password_error`, `password_required`, `negotiation_error`), detects peer `FIN` closes behind buffered unsolicited frames (`StreamReader._eof`) so idle command sessions reopen cleanly before the next write, and enforces `error::RuntimeWarning` in `pytest`.
- **Covers (`WHO = 2`) — A Partial Slat Tilt Keeps Its Angle on Position-Reporting (`Dimension 10`) Venetian Actuators ([#870](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/870), [#991](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/991))**: A position-reporting actuator counts a slat pulse as travel and reports its stopped level one step further right after the pulse's stop (`F401` behind an `F454` `2.0.51`: `*#2*21*10*10*1*001*15##`; `K4672M2S` behind a `MyHomeServer1` `2.87.13`: `*#2*31*10*10*1*001*0##`, 0.10–0.12 s after the stop). That report was read as an external level jump and turned the slats a full rotation in Home Assistant, so `set_cover_tilt_position: 15`, `25` and `50` all ended at `100 %`. A stopped level that moved the way the pulse turned, within `ECHO_WINDOW` (`1.5 s`) of the pulse's stop, is now the pulse's own: it updates `current_position` and leaves the timed angle. The claim holds for one stopped level and ends with any curtain or level command, from Home Assistant or from another client (`*#2*<WHERE>*#11#001#1*<LEVEL>##`, which now also takes the motor over from a running pulse instead of being stopped by the pulse's auto-stop). Also fixed around a pulse: a tilt reversed while the pulse runs keeps the second pulse's auto-stop when the first pulse's level arrives; `set_cover_position` to the level the blind is at stops a running pulse instead of leaving it without a stop; a blind that follows an area / group / general pulse ends at its angle when its level arrives before the scope's stop is confirmed, and takes no claim from a scope stop that was not delivered; an area run to the end takes the motor from a member's own pulse; a failed stop write is no longer logged as a never-retrieved exception. External moves are unchanged: with motion frames the slats turn in proportion to the motor time, and a level jump with no motion frame turns them to `0 %` / `100 %`. Thanks to **[@Claripinto](https://github.com/Claripinto)** for the field test on an external Venetian blind and its 60-frame trace (`tests/fixtures/traces/pr_991_myhomeserver1_k4672m2s/`).
- **Covers (`WHO = 2`) — Drift-Bounded Full-Run Settle Timer After Mid-Run Reversals ([#973](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/973), [#974](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/974), [#975](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/975))**: Timed covers (`TimedCurtainStrategy`, `VenetianTiltStrategy`) previously waited the full `travel_time + END_SETTLE_MARGIN` (`2 s`) after a mid-run reversal even when the shutter reached its limit switch much earlier, leaving Home Assistant in `opening` at `100 %` (or `closing` at `0 %`) until the entire `travel_time` elapsed. Full-run settle timers (`open_cover`, `close_cover`, `set_cover_position: 0 / 100`, scope runs, and wall runs) now query `CoverKinematicsStrategy.remaining_travel_for`, track a conservative per-cover `_position_drift_bound` (`0.5 s + 15 %` per unconfirmed partial/reversed/tilt-pulse segment, reset to `0.0` at confirmed end stops, calibrations, and bus position reports), and settle after `remaining_travel + drift_bound + END_SETTLE_MARGIN` (capped at `travel_time`) when starting from a freshly anchored intermediate position, while preserving the full `travel_time + END_SETTLE_MARGIN` wait on `unknown` positions, restored states after restart, gateway disconnects, travel/slat-time edits, saturated drift (`>= travel_time`), unopted-in custom strategies, and endpoint re-homes (`open_cover` / `100 %` at `100 %`, `close_cover` / `0 %` at `0 %`). Thanks to **[@ermanno00](https://github.com/ermanno00)** for reporting and verifying `#975` live on `MH201` (`3.3.6`) + `L4671/2` (`WHERE = 56` and the 17-member `#1` scope cover) alongside the live `MH200` (`2.1.0`) + `F422` mid-run reversal capture (`WHERE = 12#4#02`, `#974`)!
- **Covers (`WHO = 2`) — Terminal Stop Detection Inside `ECHO_WINDOW` & Automatic Pre-Move Stop on `MH201` / `MH202` Timed Actuators ([#959](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/959), [#962](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/962))**: On gateways that omit the synthetic SCS pre-move `STOP` (`12 0A`) ahead of `UP` / `DOWN` (`12 08` / `12 09`) — **`MH201`** (live `3.3.6` capture; also confirmed on `3.6.44`) and **`MH202`** (`010024` firmware oracle) — interlocked timed relay actuators (`L4671/2`, `H4671/2`, `F411/2`, `F411/4`, `F411U2`) answer an opposite command while energized (both mid-travel and during their ~60 s factory `M=0` relay cutoff after reaching a limit switch) with `*2*0*WHERE##` (`STOP`) instead of reversing, while `ECHO_WINDOW` (`1.5 s`) swallowed that `*2*0*WHERE##` and animated Home Assistant to `100 %` / `0 %` even when no `*2*1*` / `*2*2*` motor-start frame ever arrived. When a plain `*2*0*WHERE##` arrives inside `ECHO_WINDOW` and no matching motor-start status follows before the window expires, the optimistic run now aborts cleanly to stopped at its pre-command position; on `MH201` and `MH202` (and adaptively on unmeasured gateways after an unfollowed echo-window stop, or when `stop_before_move: true` is set in `myhome.yaml`), timed point and local scope covers automatically send `*2*0*WHERE##`, wait for socket delivery plus `0.6 s` (guarded by `_run_generation` against wall-switch takeovers and mid-pause `Dimension 10` promotion, with post-stop `set_cover_position` kinematics), and then send the direction frame whenever the relay may still be energized (`65 s` hold window, cleared immediately on `*2*0*WHERE##` so idle covers add zero latency or bus traffic). Thanks to **[@ermanno00](https://github.com/ermanno00)** for reporting `#959` and verifying `#962` live on an `MH201` (`3.3.6` and `3.6.44`) plant with 35× `L4671/2` shutters (single covers, the 17-member `#1` scope cover, and mixed wall-switch + HA runs)!
- **SSDP Discovery & Gateway Identity — Stop 10-Minute Reload Loop on Configured Gateways, Protect Manual & Ignored Entries & Match `Legrand S.p.A.` `F455` ([#947](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/947), [#948](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/948))**: On `v2.0.0`, every SSDP announcement or 10-minute Home Assistant SSDP scan (`SCAN_INTERVAL`) overwrote `entry.data["firmware"]` with the UPnP `modelNumber` (e.g. `"1.0"` on `MH200N`, `F454`, `F455`, `F453AV`), triggering an immediate config-entry reload (`reload_on_update`) that wrote the `WHO = 13` `Dimension 16` firmware (`*#13**16##`, e.g. `"1.1.8"`) back ~5 s later and repeated the reload cycle on the next announcement (while also risking firmware-gated `WHO = 25` / `WHO = 22` capability drops when `modelNumber` fell below the `WHO = 13` version). `_ssdp_entry_updates` now updates `CONF_HOST` (and reloads) strictly when an SSDP-discovered gateway's IP address actually changes, treats `firmware`, `friendly_name`, and `udn` as fill-if-empty (leaving `WHO = 13` `Dimension 16` authoritative and ignoring empty UPnP tags), leaves manually configured **Custom (IP Gateway)** and `SOURCE_IGNORE` entries untouched, demotes repeat `Found gateway:` logs to `DEBUG`, and adds `ST: ssdp:all` + `NT: upnp:rootdevice` SSDP matchers for `F455` gateways advertising `manufacturer = "Legrand S.p.A."`. Thanks to **[@manfredgittmaier-afk](https://github.com/manfredgittmaier-afk)** for reporting and confirming `#947` on `MH200N` (`1.1.8`) and **[@gdluck](https://github.com/gdluck)** for the fix and live `F455` (`1.0.76`) verification!
- **Thermoregulation (`WHO = 4`) — Ignore `WHERE = #0` Actuator Status Answers for Central-Unit Detection, Discovery & Routing ([#944](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/944), [#945](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/945))**: On an `F461` (FW `2.0.11`) plant without a central unit, the all-zone actuator status poll (`*#4*#0*20##`) returned `*#4*#0*20*1##` alongside per-zone actuator frames (`Z#N`), flipping `has_central_unit = True` so discovered standalone zones wrote central-addressed setpoints (`*#4*#Z*#14*TTTT*M##`) that nothing answered and lost off-season modes (`cool` while in heating). `Dimension 20` actuator status frames (both `*#4*...*20*V##` and `#20` write-form echoes) are never treated as central-unit reports on any `#` `WHERE`, `*#4*#0*20*V##` is excluded from climate bus discovery and entity routing across all valve and fan-coil output codes (`0..9`, `14..16`), and central units never queue `*#4*#0*19##` fan-coil side reads. Thanks to **[@lyubomirtraykov](https://github.com/lyubomirtraykov)** for the diagnostic trace report and **[@gdluck](https://github.com/gdluck)** for the fix!
- **Lighting (`WHO = 1`) — A Dimmer That Is On at Exact Level `0` Is Shown On, Not Off ([#970](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/970))**: A dimmer can be on and report level `0`: a physical `F418` behind an `F461` and an `F455` answered `*#1*0010##` with `*1*2*0010##` (on) and `*#1*0010*1##` with `*#1*0010*1*100*10##` (`Dimension 1`, level `0`), steadily. The entity followed the level and was shown off, so the header toggle of an entities card skipped the dimmer at the next "all off" and `light.turn_on` changed nothing. A `Dimension 1` level `0` that follows an "on" status of the light is now verified with one status request (`*#1*<where>##`): answered "on", the dimmer is shown on at the lowest level (`1 %`) and stays so; closed without an "on" status, it is off, which is what an `MH200` means by that frame after an off with a ramp (`*#1*62*1*100*2##`, then `*1*0*62##` when asked). Until the answer it is shown on only when the "on" status is at most `2 s` old; at most `3` requests in `30 s` for one light. A request that could not be made (not written, refused with a NACK, or not closed within `20 s`) leaves a dimmer already confirmed on as it is, and any other level `0` off. What says off is unchanged: the off status, a `Dimension 4` level `0` and a `Dimension 1` level `0` with no "on" status before it. See `docs/configuration/lights.md`.
- **Thermoregulation (`WHO = 4`) — Passive Second-Reading Confirmation for Unconfigured Bus Temperature Probes ([#967](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/967), [#972](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/972))**: On a 2-wire SCS bus, a single bit-7 noise flip on a zone `Dimension 0` frame (for example Zone `1` `00000001` corrupted to `129` `10000001`) shifted the address into `WHERE >= 100` (`is_probe()`), where `sensor.py` previously created a permanent `sensor.probe_129_temperature` entity whose stale reading restored via `RestoreSensor` across every Home Assistant restart, while physical external/slave probes (`3455` via `L4577`, `3475`/`3476`, `probe 303`) push autonomously and NACK explicit status polls (`9.3–9.4 s` command-session stall on `F455`, `2.1 s` on `F461`). Unconfigured `WHO = 4` bus probes (`WHERE >= 100` and `Dimension 15`) now defer creation on their first reading with **zero active polling**, suppress identical duplicate echoes within `5.0 s` (`MyHomeServer1`), expire unconfirmed single-frame candidates after `3600 s` (`1 h`), confirm on the second independent reading (distinct raw frame or `>= 5.0 s` later), isolate `F422` `#4#II` local-bus interfaces end-to-end, and canonicalize zero-padded probe addresses (`0105` → `105`) across bus, `myhome.yaml`, and entity-registry restoration, while keeping `myhome.yaml` and existing entity-registry probes immediate at startup. Thanks to **[@xmavgithub](https://github.com/xmavgithub)** for reporting the live `MyHomeServer1` (`2.87.13`) incident in Discussion `#963`!
- **Thermoregulation (`WHO = 4`) — Find Thermostats at Start Where `*#4*0##` Is Dropped, Detect Standalone Thermostats Next to a Central Unit & Check Setpoint Writes ([#951](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/951), [#955](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/955))**: On gateways that drop the general request `*#4*0##` (`F461`, `F455`, `MyHomeServer1` and others) nothing replaced it: a freshly added `F461` sent no `WHO = 4` frame at start and had no climate entity, a zone with plain valves never appeared from its held actuator frames ([#785](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/785)), and a standalone thermostat next to a central unit showed the central unit's mode and offered no `cool` until its first setpoint write. The startup sweep now asks every actuator with the published `*#4*0#0*20##` (in place of `*#4*#0*20##`) and, on `F461` and `MyHomeServer1`, the central unit with `*#4*#0##`; a zone known only from plain valves is asked for its temperature (`*#4*Z*0##`), one at a time on a quiet bus. A zone found on the bus that reports the season the central unit is not in is read again (`*#4*Z*12##`) and, when it reports that season a second time, becomes a standalone thermostat (attribute `standalone_detected`) written with the direct form `*#4*Z*#14*TTTT*M##`; a later report of the central unit about the zone puts it back. A setpoint written through the central unit (`*#4*#Z*#14*TTTT*M##`) is checked against what the plant reports, and a write the zone did not take or the gateway refused (NACK) fails the service call instead of leaving a dial that jumps back. A zone found on the bus offers `cool` once the bus shows that it cools, and shows the same state, action and modes as the same zone configured in `myhome.yaml`. A zone switched off and on again before its actuator had stopped no longer stays `idle` while the actuator runs: an actuator that was only assumed off is asked once the zone runs. Run live on `F461` (FW `2.0.11`), `F455` (FW `1.0.76`), `MyHomeServer1` (FW `3.87.13`) and `3488` (FW `3.2.5`); details in `docs/configuration/climate.md`.
- **Thermoregulation (`WHO = 4`) — Central Unit `heat` / `cool` Leave Protection, Errors Instead of Silent No-Ops, the Commanded Setpoint Kept Across Protection and Restarts, Slave Probe Reads & `3550` Battery Repair `Ignore` ([#983](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/983))**: what changes for a user:
    - **Upgrade note (`2.0.0` → `2.0.1`, first start)**: `nominal_temperature` (the commanded setpoint a zone goes back to) is new, so a zone that was `off`, in antifreeze or in thermal protection when Home Assistant stopped under `2.0.0` has none saved. Until that zone reports its commanded setpoint (dimension 14) or a temperature is set, `climate.set_hvac_mode` with `heat` / `cool` fails with `zone_no_setpoint_known` ("has not reported a setpoint yet: set a temperature first") and sends nothing; `climate.set_temperature` works at once. An automation that switches such a zone on right after the upgrade should set a temperature first.
    - **Central unit `#0` (99 zones)**: `heat` / `cool` send the season frame (`*4*1*#0##` / `*4*0*#0##`) and, when the central unit has reported protection, off or the other season since Home Assistant started, follow it with `*4*3100*#0##`, so the `3550` starts the last weekly program of that season instead of staying in protection (live `F461` + `F455`, 2026-11-18). The call fails when the gateway refuses either frame, does not write it or does not confirm it. A 4-zone central unit (`#0#N`), and a central unit that has not reported since Home Assistant started, get the season frame only.
    - **`auto` is not passed on to the zones**: the central unit shows `auto` only until it reports and then `heat` / `cool`; its zones keep the mode they show (a zone on the central unit's program is `heat` / `cool` with `zone_operation: automatic`). Up to `2.0.0` every zone of the central unit that was not off was shown `auto` until its next report.
    - **Commanded setpoint**: while a zone is `off` the slider shows the protection setpoint and `nominal_temperature` the setpoint it goes back to; `heat` / `cool` write that setpoint, also after a restart. A zone command the gateway refuses now fails the service call (`zone_command_refused`) instead of being shown as done.
    - **Central unit name**: a central unit found on the bus is named "Central Unit 0" from the start (`climate.central_unit_0` on a fresh install); it was "Climate Zone 0" until the first restart. An entity that already exists keeps its id.
    - **Probes**: a slave probe (`PZZ`) that has sent nothing for 15 minutes is asked on dimension 0 (an external probe `N00` on dimension 15); a refusal stops the read until the gateway that served it reconnects or another gateway serves the read (a delegated secondary, the warm standby, the primary when it is back).
    - **`myhome.yaml`, central unit**: `zone: "0"` is the 99-zone central unit `#0`, with or without `central: true`. `2.0.0` filed `zone: "0"` with `central: true` under `#0#0`, an address no central unit has. Its saved entity keeps its entity id and its device (name, area) and becomes the central unit `#0`; where the central unit found on the bus is saved as well, that one stays and the `#0#0` entity is removed (the name and the area given to its device go to the device that stays, where that one has none of its own). The same holds for `zone: "#0#1"` with `central: true`, which `2.0.0` filed under `#0##0#1`, and for an interface written in the zone (`zone: "0#4#01"`). The copy of `myhome.yaml` kept in the entry options is corrected too.
    - **`myhome.yaml`, zones**: a zone written `#1` or `01` beside a 4-zone central unit (`zone: "1"`, `central: true`) keeps its number; `001` (all the probes of zone 1) is not another spelling of zone 1.
    - **Zone state**: a manual-with-setpoint report of a 4-zone central unit about one of its zones ends the antifreeze that zone showed (the case of [#994](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/994)); `running_fan_speed` `off` from the fan speed `15` of dimension 11 ends when the zone reports a speed again, and an `off` from the zone's valve report stays.
    - **Thermo actuator switch**: a dimension 20 frame for the bare zone proves no actuator number, so a whole-zone switch keeps writing the whole zone until an actuator reports; a central unit's WHERE (`#Z`, `#0#N`) is not taken for the zone, and a WHERE that is neither the zone nor one of its actuators changes nothing. A whole-zone off puts the output levels the whole-zone switch shows at 0.
    - **`3550` battery repair**: `Ignore` on `central_battery_fault` holds through every status burst and reload until Home Assistant restarts ([#846](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/846), [#884](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/issues/884)).
- **Lighting (`WHO = 1`) — Read a Light Back When Its Status Does Not Follow an Acknowledged Command ([#964](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/964))**: An `F455` (firmware `1.0.76`) leaves status frames out of its event session when several lights answer close together: with six lights switched by one `light.turn_on` / `light.turn_off` call it left out one or two statuses in 5 of 8 steps, while an `F461` on the same bus relayed all of them. A plain light takes its state only from that frame, so Home Assistant showed the old state, and the header toggle of an entities card, which only commands the entities not yet shown in the target state, left such a light on at the next "all off". On every gateway model (the read-back does not look at the model; the `F455` is where the loss was measured), the gateway handler (`gateway_confirm.py`) now notes every acknowledged point-to-point `WHO = 1` command and, when no matching status of that light arrived `1.5 s` later, sends one status request `*#1*<where>##`; nothing is sent where the status arrives. Not used for group / area / general commands, exposed addresses or `WHO = 2` covers; a burst sent by another client is not read back (see `docs/configuration/runtime_behaviour.md`).

#### ⚙️ CI & Tooling

- **Home Assistant `2026.12+` `DeviceInfo` Mapping AST Guard Across `tests/` & Trace Metadata ([#954](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/954), [#953](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/953))**: Extended the AST-based `DeviceInfo` mapping-access guard (`home-assistant/core#192323`) across `tests/` and alias forms so dict-style `device_info` reads fail fast locally on Home Assistant `<= 2026.10`, and documented standalone zone `2` vs `3550`-managed zones `3`–`4` in the `central_restore_3100_live_2026-11-12` trace fixture.
- **GitHub Actions Pin Updates ([#943](https://github.com/OpenWebNet-HA/MyHOME/pull/943))**: Updated SHA-pinned GitHub Actions across repository workflows (`crowdin/github-action` `v3.6.0`, `actions/setup-python` `v7.1.0`, `docker/login-action` `v4.8.0`, and `actions/upload-artifact` `v7.0.2`).
